floor_history.headline: recon: honest floor 48 -> 47 (xor operand order); residual attributed to sched1 block-5 multiply order (~38), un-coalesced dist copy into $a0 (~5, sibling func_8002D518's closed residual), and reorg s
Structural: honest floor 47 -> 10/202 — named cross-product locals per side test (-24), centroid term first in the XOR with the locals reused across tests (-9), sibling LZCS clobber footprint $12-$15
Floor 10 -> 7/202: the tail residual is CLOSED by an if/return-0 block-structure change, which unlocked the s2-banked LZCR slot operand; residual A is now an allocation question, not a schedule.

First faithful permuter workspace for func_8002D780 built and validated; 55,531-iteration campaign found nothing — its metric is anti-correlated with the engine's on this chassis — and nine embedded-a
Floor 7 -> 2/202: residual B closed (the dist copy survives cse only when the carrier is multiply-defined AND declared before lzcr) and the LZCR slot-address order closed by splitting the LZCS island

Residual A fully attributed from the dumps: it is one local-alloc qty_compare_1 TIE (dz and dx both 3 refs / 7 insns in the target's emission order), not a scheduling wall; 37 variants in four batches

Solver typed both halves of the last 2 insns: sched is solvable (180/720 statement orders reach the target's emission order) but on that order local-alloc sees dz and dx tied on every qty_compare_1 in

Forensics closed the sched1 side of residual A as a class kill (LUID is the only C-side input) and killed two of the three spellings of the local-alloc-time artifact the target needs: a self-assign em

Read local-alloc's own allocation trace: the residual-A seat flip IS reachable by one extra short-lived block-7 quantity (proved in probe u3's QTYDBG trace), but the only live range that outranks dz w

frontier.hypothesis: The extra block-7 quantity the target needs is a cross-block copy carrier whose copy insn lands at block-7 insn 2 (between ax's subu and dz's subu) with refs 2, birth 4 and death 8, and which is then deleted by jump2's delete_noop_moves so build_insns stays at 202.
frontier.mechanism: s9 pinned the unique admissible live range (refs 2 / birth 4 / death 8: above dz's 2500, below ax's 5000, conflicting with dz, clear of dx's birth at 8). s8 established that a copy surviving cse needs its second definition in a different basic block, and that jump_optimize is passed noop_moves == 1 only at the jump2 call (toplev.c:3142), i.e. after local_alloc has already counted the quantity.
frontier.next_probe: Build an `m`-shaped carrier on the h1 order (declared before the test-2 arm, defined once inside that arm from a statement test 2 already needs -- s8 batch R showed manufacturing that definition costs +7/+11 -- and re-assigned inside test 3 from a value that dies at the copy). BEFORE scoring, run tmp/grind/func_8002D780/s9/dumpvar.py with BB2_CC1=tools/gcc-2.7.2/cc1 and confirm in the blk=7 SUGGDBG-QTY table that the new quantity reports birth 4 death 8 refs 2 and that ax still reports birth 2 death 6; only then score, requiring build_insns == 202.

frontier.hypothesis: Removing ax from block_alloc's competition (making it a multi-block pseudo seated by global_alloc) lets the u3-shaped extra quantity take $v0 without displacing anything, so the dz/dx seats flip on the h1 order at no register cost.
frontier.mechanism: u3 already proves the seat flip; its entire cost is that ax loses $v0 to the new quantity. block_alloc only allocates pseudos whose live range lies inside one basic block (local-alloc.c:470-478), so a multi-block ax is skipped and its seat comes from global.c instead. s6's batch O did exactly this to dz and dx (23-40) but never to ax.
frontier.next_probe: Carry `ax` (= cx - x0) in a variable that is also live in the test-2 block, on the h1 statement order, with and without the u3-shaped extra value; read the blk=7 SUGGDBG-QTY table first to confirm ax has left the quantity list and that dz/dx are seated $a0/$v1, then score and check build_insns.

frontier.hypothesis: A decomp-permuter campaign on the 2-floor chassis finds the last two instructions where the s4 campaign on the 7-floor chassis found nothing.
frontier.mechanism: s7 typed the residual as a local-alloc tie, s8 class-killed the sched1 side, and s9 has now reduced the whole remaining search to introducing one extra short-lived temporary in one block -- which is precisely the permuter's temporary-introduction and statement-reordering move set. The s4 campaign's neighbourhood was dominated by residuals B and C, both now closed.
frontier.next_probe: Regenerate base.c from memory/grind/func_8002D780/candidate.c AND from the h1 body into the validated workspace tmp/grind/func_8002D780/s4/nonmatchings/func_8002D780 (four hurdles + rebuild recipe in evidence.md [s4]), launch with tools/permuter_campaign.py, wait IN-TURN with `permuter_campaign.py wait --dir <ws>`, harvest with --stop before the turn ends, and re-score every find on the engine sandbox (the s4 finding that the permuter's weighted metric is anti-correlated with the engine's here still applies).
